newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan passenger traffic on Israel route rises.
newsitem.headline: Jordan passenger traffic on Israel route rises.

text.p: Jordan's Royal Wings regional carrier's passenger traffic has been steadily increasing on its regular Amman-Tel Aviv route since it became operational a year ago, a company official said on Monday.

The airline's marketing and sales manager Amar Balkr told Reuters that 18,100 passengers were carried on its Amman-Tel Aviv flights from April last year, when it began its service, until the end of last month.
Royal Wings, a subsidiary of national carrier Royal Jordanian (RJ), inaugurated its first commercial flights on the route in April 1996, using two 50 seater turbo-prop Canadian built Dash planes.

Israel's mainly Arkia domestic operator followed two months later with a similar five times a week service stipulated for each national carrier under a transport accord signed within the framework of a peace accord between with the two countries in 1994.

The air links between the two neighbours were expanded recently to a new twice weekly service Haifa-Amman expected to be fully operational this month and an extra sixth flight between Amman and Tel Aviv launched early this year.
The seat factor rose from around 40-45 percent in the few months after the start fo the service to around 63-65 percent currently, Balkr said.
Jordan is restricted to a current 450 passengers ceiling per week stipulated under the accord.
Royal Wings also said 49,402 passengers were carried on board its Amman-Aqaba service since it introduced the 14 times a week flights last October to capitalise on increasing demand in tourism.
Royal Wings was to operate 25 charter flights during this month for both domestic and international tourist traffic from Amman to Egyptian Red Sea resorts, the airline official addded.
The company is also studying a regular route from Cyprus to Jordan during the peak summer period, Balkr said.
